review.summary: I reviewed only the supplied migration and the two source writers. I did not review or certify the omitted auth, proof, runtime or test code, and none of this counts as fullWP or release acceptance. The DB-side binding behaves as described. It requires the same tenant, live, version, run and kind, and each frame can be used once. It sits after the original guards, keeps the legacy no-run path, and has no backfill. I found two issues. MAJOR: once a run exists, any source write without a frame binding fails with a raw error, so a run that has been stopped while its version stays enabled could block playback. MINOR: a binding minted for an older version may still throw in the playback path instead of returning null.

findings.area: resolveTrackedLivePlaybackSource intake INSERT (and issueMetricVisitPage INSERT/catch in src/lib/live-metric-visit-page.ts); trigger NOT FOUND/frame branch in migration.sql
findings.issue: Once a run exists for the selected version, every source write without a binding fails, and neither writer turns that failure into a defined outcome. In the playback path the 23514 error is thrown out of the transaction as a raw error and the viewer is denied playback. In the visit-page path it becomes a thrown PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE.
findings.evidence: The trigger runs the frame lookup whenever a run row is found. If ingressFrameId is NULL the lookup finds nothing, so it raises 'metric ingress source requires admitted frame'. The app-side requireMetricIngressSource has no tx or run visibility, so an undefined binding passes it. resolveTrackedLivePlaybackSource has no catch, and the visit-page catch maps only SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE/LIFETIME_UNAVAILABLE/expired/P2090 to null. The scope says 'Stop closes admission' but does not say the collection version is disabled. After a stop no new frames can be minted, yet resolveMetricPlaybackContext can still return the run-owned version.
findings.impact: Metric-collection state can change whether playback is allowed: 'Playback authorization stays canonical' no longer holds. After a stop, or for any caller or path that does not supply a frame, every viewer of that live could get a failed playback or page render instead of the canonical response. This lasts until the version expires or changes.
findings.recommended_fix: In the writer transaction, after the version lock and context check, look up whether a run exists. If it does and there is no valid binding, return a defined, documented result, for example the same null used for context races, or an explicit no-intake path agreed in scope. Do not let 23514 escape. Alternatively, make Stop end or disable the version's collection lifetime so resolve*Context returns null. Either way, write down the post-stop behavior explicitly.
findings.required_test: On a disposable DB, create a run on an enabled version, then stop it while keeping the version enabled. Call resolveTrackedLivePlaybackSource and issueMetricVisitPage without a binding. Assert the documented outcome (null or defined untracked behavior) rather than a raw or 500 error, and assert that no intake or page row is written.

findings.area: requireMetricIngressSource call after the current/context version check
findings.issue: The race fix only covers the case where both context and current are null. If a binding was minted for version V1 and the stable context and current version are both V2, requireMetricIngressSource throws. Its error class lives in the omitted module, and this path has no catch. A stale binding may therefore still surface as an authorization error or exception instead of the null used for other context races.
findings.evidence: `if (!context && !current) { if(binding)return null; ...}` and `if (!current || current.versionId !== context.versionId) return null;` both run before `requireMetricIngressSource(binding,{...versionId:current.versionId},['playback'])`. Nothing compares binding.versionId to current.versionId before that call.
findings.impact: Similar version-switch races get different outcomes. A stale binding could produce a not_authorized or 500 response for a viewer whose admission is still valid. No source is mis-bound, because both the app check and the DB still reject it.
findings.recommended_fix: Before calling requireMetricIngressSource, compare the binding's scope/version with current. On mismatch, return null the same way as other context races. Or confirm that requireMetricIngressSource throws a type that is mapped to null.
findings.required_test: Mint a binding for V1, switch the enabled version to V2, then call resolveTrackedLivePlaybackSource with that binding. Assert it returns null, writes no intake row, and does not throw MetricIngestError('not_authorized').
